# phase-091 — Document the memory model: shared values, copying, and the cycle leak

## You must change `docs/ or README.md`

This phase declares `must_touch: [docs/ or README.md]`. The gate fails the phase unless at
least one changed file falls under it. Writing tests, documentation or a report
is not enough — if you finish without touching that area, the phase fails on
exactly that check.


## Evidence — verified finding

```
The memory model is a real and deliberate design, and it is documented nowhere a user would look. src/value.rs:276 defines `pub type Shared<T> = std::sync::Arc<T>`, and Value::List, Value::Record and Value::Object (src/value.rs:253-255) are Arc-shared, so they are immutable once built. Reading a variable clones the value bound to it (src/value.rs:88-90), so assignment copies rather than aliases. Two consequences follow and neither is written down. First, Arc drops when the last reference goes and no Weak appears anywhere in src/, so a reference cycle is never collected and leaks - a real limitation that will surface eventually as an unexplained memory growth bug. Second, there is no tracing garbage collector and no ownership or borrowing rule a Redblue programmer must learn, which is a feature for a language whose goal is plain-English readability and a cost in that it is copying rather than zero-cost.
```

**Re-verify this before you change anything.** If the finding no longer
reproduces on `main`, stop and write that to `FINDINGS.md` — a stale phase must
never be "fixed" by inventing a change.

## Goal

Write MEMORY.md stating the model exactly as implemented: values are immutable and Arc-shared, reading copies, there is no garbage collector, there is no cycle collection, and a cycle therefore leaks. Document the cycle leak as a known limitation with the shape of program that triggers it, not as a defect to be fixed later. Also document that deep recursion is bounded by MAX_CALL_DEPTH and raises a catchable Error::Limit rather than overflowing the native stack (src/bytecode/vm.rs:18-21 asserts 'There is no path from a .rbc to a native stack overflow'), and that REDBLUE_MAX_CALL_DEPTH overrides it. Link it from README.md. Implement nothing.

## Definition of done

- [ ] MEMORY.md states that values are immutable once constructed and shared, and cites src/value.rs:276 by line
- [ ] MEMORY.md states that reading a variable copies rather than aliases, citing src/value.rs:88-90
- [ ] MEMORY.md names the absence of cycle collection as a known limitation and gives a Redblue program that leaks because of it
- [ ] MEMORY.md documents MAX_CALL_DEPTH as a catchable Error::Limit with the REDBLUE_MAX_CALL_DEPTH override, citing src/bytecode/vm.rs
- [ ] README.md links MEMORY.md
